newsitem.title: UK: New food scare hits Britain.
newsitem.headline: New food scare hits Britain.

text.p: The British government advised parents on Friday to wash and peel fruit after tests revealed contaminated peaches and apples containing up to four times the recommended level of pesticides.

The fruit problem follows scares over the safety of pre-prepared meats and public concern over Mad Cow disease. Polls show widespread distrust of the government following the fatal food scares, and the fracas over fruit will do little to enhance its image with consumers.
The government was quick to insist there was no cause for concern.

"Levels of residues in the majority of fruit and vegetables fall well below maximum residue levels. However, a small number of apples and peaches, including imports, had higher residue levels than desirable," it said in a statement.
It said Britain would press for worldwide action to improve the monitoring of pesticides.
Recent food scares have centred on meat, even though the government insists British beef is safe to eat.
But with fear of Mad Cow disease still widespread, it has also admitted that slaughterhouses have broken rules in the past and is currently facing criticism about hygiene in abattoirs.
Poor hygiene can lead to food poisoning, such as the E coli outbreak that killed 18 people in Scotland this year and last.
